items.title: Image-Guided Biopsies to Study Resistance to Lu-177-PSMA Therapy
items.summary: This phase 1 trial uses image-guided biopsies to understand why Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy stops working in some metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. By studying tumor tissue during treatment, doctors hope to learn how cancer cells develop resistance and plan better treatments in the future.

items.title: Real-World Use of Hormone-Blocking Drugs in Australian Prostate Cancer Patients
items.summary: This observational study examines how androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (like enzalutamide, apalutamide, and abiraterone) are used in real-world practice for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients in Australia. The research analyzes prescription data to understand treatment patterns and patient outcomes outside of clinical trials.

items.title: Comparing Hormone-Blocking Drugs in Castrate-Sensitive Prostate Cancer Veterans
items.summary: This phase 2 trial in Veterans Affairs hospitals compares three hormone-blocking drugs (abiraterone, enzalutamide, and apalutamide) in castrate-sensitive prostate cancer. The study aims to validate real-world effectiveness measurements and understand how treatment choices affect survival in veterans with various health conditions.

items.title: Testing Actinium-225 Radioligand Therapy for Advanced Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests BAY3546828, a radioactive drug that binds to cancer proteins to deliver targeted radiation in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study evaluates safety, how the drug moves through the body, and early signs of effectiveness in patients who have exhausted other treatments.

items.title: Lu-177 PSMA Therapy in mCRPC Patients With Kidney Impairment
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies whether kidney problems affect how lutetium-177 vipivotide tetraxetan (Pluvicto) works in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study examines drug distribution, radiation dosing, safety, and heart rhythm effects in patients with moderate to severe kidney impairment compared to those with normal kidney function.

items.title: Talazoparib With or Without Enzalutamide After Abiraterone Treatment
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether adding talazoparib (a PARP inhibitor) to enzalutamide, or using talazoparib alone, delays cancer progression in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients with HRR gene mutations who previously received abiraterone. The study focuses on patients with specific DNA repair defects.

items.title: Real-World Darolutamide Study in Indian Non-Metastatic CRPC Patients
items.summary: This phase 4 study examines how darolutamide plus androgen deprivation therapy performs in real-world Indian patients with high-risk non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial evaluates safety and effectiveness outside of controlled clinical trial settings in this specific population.

items.title: Validating Drug Targets for Antibody-Drug Conjugates in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This observational study evaluates 15 protein targets (including PSMA, B7-H3, and HER2) that could be used for antibody-drug conjugate therapies in different types of prostate cancer. Researchers examine tumor tissue to determine which targets are present and whether they predict patient survival across various disease stages.

items.title: Immunotherapy Plus Cabozantinib for Rare Genitourinary Cancers
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests combining cabozantinib (a targeted therapy) with two immunotherapy drugs (nivolumab and ipilimumab) in patients with rare genitourinary tumors that have spread. The study includes some prostate cancer subtypes and aims to determine if this triple combination is more effective than single agents.

items.title: Early Testing of RO7656594 in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates the safety, optimal dosing, and early effectiveness of RO7656594, a new experimental drug for advanced or metastatic prostate cancer. The study aims to determine recommended doses for future trials and assess how the drug is processed in the body.

items.title: Single-Dose MRI-Guided Radiation for Recurrent Prostate Cancer in Lymph Nodes
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies whether a single high-dose radiation treatment guided by MRI can safely treat prostate cancer that has returned in a limited number of pelvic or abdominal lymph nodes. The trial evaluates side effects, tumor control, time until hormone therapy is needed, and quality of life.

items.title: Personalized Treatment Approach for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests a personalized treatment strategy where therapy intensity is matched to disease risk, followed by treatment de-escalation when appropriate. The study evaluates whether this approach maintains cancer control while reducing treatment-related side effects and improving quality of life in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients.

items.title: Safety Study of Xaluritamig in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates the safety profile of xaluritamig, a new investigational drug, in adult patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study focuses on determining whether the proposed treatment regimen is safe and well-tolerated.

items.title: Chemotherapy Plus Immunotherapy Followed by PARP Inhibitor for Aggressive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests a sequence of treatments for aggressive variant metastatic prostate cancer: first chemotherapy (cabazitaxel and carboplatin) plus immunotherapy (cetrelimab), followed by maintenance therapy with niraparib (a PARP inhibitor) with or without continued immunotherapy. The study evaluates this combination approach in hard-to-treat aggressive disease.

items.title: Prostate and Metastasis Radiation for Incomplete Hormone Therapy Response
items.summary: This trial studies whether adding radiation to the prostate and visible metastases improves outcomes in newly metastatic prostate cancer patients whose PSA remains elevated after six months of dual hormone therapy. The study targets patients with incomplete response to hormone treatment and at least four bone metastases.

items.title: Pre-Surgery Study of PARP Inhibitor Plus Enzalutamide in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates adding talazoparib (a PARP inhibitor) to standard hormone therapy and enzalutamide before surgery in prostate cancer patients with lymph node spread. The study assesses effectiveness of this combination in treating locally advanced disease before surgical removal.

items.title: Testing AZD0516 Alone and Combined in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates AZD0516, a new investigational drug, both alone and in combination with other anti-cancer agents for metastatic prostate cancer. The study assesses safety, tolerability, and early signs of effectiveness of this experimental treatment.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone for Chemotherapy-Naive mCRPC
items.summary: This pivotal phase 3 trial compares overall survival in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients receiving xaluritamig plus abiraterone versus standard treatments (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone alone). The study focuses on patients who have not yet received chemotherapy for their metastatic disease.

items.title: HER2-Targeted Armed Cell Therapy for Metastatic Breast and Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests HER2 FPBMC, a treatment where patient immune cells are armed with antibodies targeting HER2 protein on cancer cells. Patients with metastatic breast or prostate cancer receive multiple infusions, and the study evaluates safety and early effectiveness of this novel cell-based approach.

items.title: Radium-223 With DNA Repair Inhibitor and/or Immunotherapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial compares three approaches for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: radium-223 alone, radium-223 plus M3814 (a DNA repair inhibitor), or the combination of all three with avelumab (immunotherapy). The study determines optimal dosing and compares effectiveness of these treatment strategies.

items.title: Dual-Target CAR-NK Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests ETB-DualNK-01, an experimental therapy using engineered natural killer cells that target both PSMA and PSCA proteins on prostate cancer cells. The study evaluates safety and early anti-tumor activity in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients, with dose escalation to find the optimal treatment level.

items.title: Carboplatin Study in Metastatic Prostate Cancer With DNA Repair Defects
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial evaluated whether carboplatin chemotherapy works effectively in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients whose tumors have defects in homologous recombination DNA repair genes. The study aimed to identify which molecular abnormalities predict response to platinum-based chemotherapy.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Radium-223 for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer With Bone Metastases
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial studies the best dose and effectiveness of combining olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) with radium-223 (a bone-targeted radiation) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients with bone metastases. The study evaluates safety and whether this combination improves treatment outcomes.

items.title: Combined Actinium-225 and Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy for Progressive mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests combining two radioactive treatments that target PSMA on prostate cancer cells: Ac-225-J591 and Lu-177-PSMA. By delivering different types of radiation together, the study aims to find a safe and effective dose combination for progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: Tinengotinib Combined With Standard Treatments for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates whether tinengotinib combined with either abiraterone/prednisone or enzalutamide is safe and causes few side effects in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study tests this investigational drug added to standard hormone-blocking therapies.

items.title: Early Testing of GDC-1261 in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates GDC-1261, an experimental drug, in patients with advanced or metastatic prostate cancer. The study assesses safety, how the drug is processed in the body, early signs of activity, and determines recommended doses for future studies.

items.title: Lead-212 Radioligand Therapy for GRPR-Expressing Tumors Including Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This first-in-human phase 1 trial tests Pb-212-DOTAM-GRPR1, a radioactive treatment targeting gastrin-releasing peptide receptors found on some prostate cancers and other tumors. The study evaluates safety, optimal dosing, radiation distribution, and early effectiveness in patients with metastatic disease.

items.title: How Inflammation Drives Treatment Resistance in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research paper explains how chronic inflammation rewires prostate cancer cells at the molecular level, promoting treatment resistance, immune evasion, and metastasis. The study describes how inflammatory pathways (NFκB and IL-6/JAK/STAT3) interact with androgen receptor signaling to drive castration-resistant disease progression.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immunotherapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study tested a next-generation DNA vaccine targeting PSMA that stimulates immune responses against prostate cancer. When combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade immunotherapy, the vaccine increased effectiveness by enhancing immune system activation, reducing regulatory T cells, and preventing metastasis in animal models.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes c-MYC-Driven Resistance in mCRPC
items.summary: Researchers developed a new drug (compound 21d) that simultaneously blocks two cancer-promoting pathways (BRD4 and AKT) to overcome treatment resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This dual inhibitor addresses the problem of c-MYC oncogene elevation that causes resistance to AKT inhibitors alone.

items.title: Overview of Theranostics in Nuclear Medicine Practice
items.summary: This review article summarizes how radioactive treatments paired with diagnostic imaging (theranostics) have evolved from specialized practice to mainstream cancer care, particularly with Lu-177 treatments for neuroendocrine tumors and PSMA-positive prostate cancer. The article provides practical guidance for nuclear medicine physicians on trial design and preparing practices for expanding treatments.

items.title: Current State of PSMA Theranostics in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review discusses the paradigm shift brought by PSMA-based imaging and treatment in prostate cancer management. PSMA-ligand PET/CT has shown superior diagnostic accuracy compared to conventional imaging, and phase 3 evidence supports PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy effectiveness across various clinical settings.

items.title: Single-Scan Dosimetry for Lu-177-PSMA Therapy Predicts Treatment Outcomes
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This study of 59 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients found that automated radiation dose measurements from a single scan after Lu-177-PSMA treatment can predict blood count changes and treatment response. Bone marrow radiation dose correlated with blood cell decreases, PSA response, and overall outcomes.

items.title: Lu-177-PSMA Therapy Equally Effective in Younger Prostate Cancer Patients
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This matched-pair analysis compared Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy outcomes between younger (≤65) and older (≥70) prostate cancer patients. Both age groups showed similar effectiveness in PSA reduction, progression-free survival, and overall survival, with comparable safety profiles, supporting treatment use in younger patients.

items.title: Machine Learning Predicts Survival in Non-Surgical Prostate Cancer With Bone Metastases
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: Researchers developed machine learning models using data from over 3,300 patients to predict survival in non-surgical prostate cancer patients with bone metastases. The model identified Gleason score as the most important survival predictor, more important than cancer stage, suggesting treatment should prioritize aggressive therapy for high-grade tumors.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This comprehensive analysis of 21 clinical trials involving 1,580 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients found that immune checkpoint inhibitors show modest benefit overall, with combination therapies performing better than single or dual immunotherapy. The study highlights preliminary but encouraging results when immunotherapy is combined with other treatments.

items.title: Zoledronic Acid Protects Bone During Hormone Plus Enzalutamide Treatment
items.summary: The BonEnza phase 2 trial found that adding zoledronic acid to hormone therapy plus enzalutamide significantly protected bone density in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients. After 18 months, patients receiving zoledronic acid had better bone mineral density and quality scores compared to those without bone-protective therapy.
